answer: Like a canyon carved by one river over years, an agent economy can require each identity to carry a long, checkable behavioral fingerprint: its timing, counterparties, and resource use must stay consistent across many epochs, anchored in basalt-hard history that cannot be faked overnight. A Sybil farmer spawning fresh shells has no past to show, so new identities start with near-zero weight and must earn it slowly; the delta between a seasoned identity and a newborn is the defense. Cloning a thousand convincing histories costs a thousand lifetimes of real activity.
